rubriker.title: Fagernes: Gloeckler holds outright lead with three rounds to go
rubriker._rss_content: Christian Gloeckler is the sole leader of the Fagernes International Autumn after seven rounds. The 14-year-old German IM defeated Lukas Dotzer on Thursday to reach 6/7, while Rinat Jumabayev beat top seed Elham Amar to move into clear second place on 5½ points. Gloeckler and Jumabayev have already met, as they drew their round-four encounter after 84 moves. | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

rubriker.title: The 2026/27 season of the Bundesliga kicks off this weekend
rubriker._rss_content: The Chess Bundesliga, a.k.a. German League, kicks off its 2026/27 season this coming weekend. Last season's champions SC Viernheim and OSG Baden-Baden are the favourites to win the title. SV Erkenschwick 1923 will be making their debut in the league, while the other two promoted teams from the second division - SF Bad Mergentheim and SC Remagen Sinzig - have already competed in the top flight. Bundesliga fans can look forward to comprehensive live commentary throughout the coming season. | Pictured: OSG Baden-Baden's Viswanathan Anand and Vincent Keymer | Photo: Stefan Liebig

Fabiano Caruana targets fifth consecutive US title
rubriker._rss_content: Fabiano Caruana has won the US Championship five times, including four consecutive titles from 2022 to 2025. His first victory came on his debut in 2016, shortly after returning to the US federation. At the 2026 edition in Saint Louis, Caruana can equal Samuel Reshevsky’s record of five consecutive titles and, with a sixth overall win, draw level with Walter Browne on the all-time list. | Photo: Lennart Ootes

rubriker.title: Beating the Sicilian with 3.Bc4 - seriously?
rubriker._rss_content: This is not an advertisement! The 'amateur move' 3.Bc4 (without a subsequent d2-d4) against the Sicilian Defence, combined with a setup resembling the Italian Game, is becoming increasingly popular. Even top professionals are now using this system successfully, first in online blitz and now also in classical over-the-board games. At the Chess Olympiad, Michael Adams used it to defeat Etienne Bacrot. | Photo: Michal Walusza

rubriker.title: President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev receives FIDE President Timur Turlov
rubriker._rss_content: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has met newly elected FIDE President Timur Turlov to discuss the development of chess in the country and future cooperation with FIDE. Their talks covered chess in education, coach and arbiter training, youth development and the organisation of major events. Tokayev also highlighted Kazakhstan's recent progress, including the women's team'’s silver medal at the Samarkand Olympiad and the growing number of active players nationwide. | Photo: FIDE

rubriker.title: Frederik Svane: An understated Olympic record
rubriker._rss_content: Two Olympiads, thirteen wins, seven draws, no defeats, two individual gold medals and a team bronze - Frederik Svane's Olympiad record is impressive. At the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, he also set a low-key record: never before had a German player won two Olympiad gold medals for the best performance on his board. | Photo: Nils Rohde

rubriker.title: Did Malcolm Pein's Endorsement Help Turlov Win FIDE?
rubriker._rss_content: The suspicion that has trailed Timur Turlov's election as FIDE president since the Samarkand General Assembly has now reached the business press. Business Matters, a UK outlet, published a piece on October 9 asking whether the endorsement of English chess figure Malcolm Pein helped put a candidate under Ukrainian sanctions at the head of the world federation.

rubriker.title: Magnus Carlsen to launch new elite tournament in Barcelona
rubriker._rss_content: Magnus Carlsen is coming to Barcelona on October 20 to unveil the MOVE Cup, a new elite tournament set to debut January 18-20, 2027. rubriker.title: «El ajedrez quizás sea uno de los deportes menos expresivos que he visto en mi vida»
rubriker._rss_content: Acostumbrada al bádminton y al automovilismo, Naganethra Reddy esperaba que el ajedrez le pareciera silencioso y difícil de interpretar. Sin embargo, su experiencia como espectadora de la Global Chess League cambió esa percepción: el dramatismo se encontraba en las miradas, las pausas y los pequeños gestos alrededor del tablero, así como en las historias que se contaban durante los comentarios de las partidas. Estas son sus impresiones. | En la imagen: Bibisara Assaubayeva | Foto: Global Chess League 2026

rubriker.title: Las piezas de ajedrez más antiguas del mundo
rubriker._rss_content: En 1977, el historiador y arqueólogo Yuri Buryakov descubrió siete piezas de marfil en las ruinas de la antigua ciudad de Afrasiab, cerca de Samarcanda. Las piezas han sido datadas a mediados del siglo VII y se consideran las piezas de ajedrez más antiguas conocidas en el mundo. | Foto: Museo Estatal de Samarcanda
